PROBLEM: When an agent run ends, especially abnormally, there must be a complete, typed record of what happened for debugging, auditing, and downstream decisions.
MECHANISM: src/minisweagent/agents/default.py serializes the full trajectory (model stats, config, agent type, version, exit status, submission, full messages, environment/model serialization, format version) and saves it in a finally block after every iteration, so even crashed runs leave a record. Exit statuses are typed: limits, timeouts, repeated format errors, and exceptions with traceback are distinct outcomes, not a generic failure. Batch runner (src/minisweagent/run/benchmarks/swebench.py) uses one isolated environment per instance, a thread pool, a lock-protected preds.json, clears stale prior outputs before rerun, and saves the per-instance trajectory even on failure.
INVARIANT: Every run leaves a trajectory, including failed ones. Exit reasons are typed; unknown failures cannot masquerade as known ones.
FAILURE_MODEL: finally-block persistence guarantees a record on crash. Typed exits let downstream logic distinguish retryable (timeout) from terminal (repeated format errors) from bug (exception). Stale outputs are cleared before rerun so old results cannot be mistaken for new ones.
SECURITY_MODEL: Per-instance isolated environments; lock-protected shared prediction file prevents torn writes.
SCALING_MODEL: Thread-pool parallelism with per-instance isolation; trajectory files are per-instance and independent.
CRX_ANALOG: Every worker execution emits a typed completion event (success, limit, timeout, format-error, exception) with a trajectory artifact ref; stale outputs are tombstoned before retry so receipts are never ambiguous.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX types the exit taxonomy into its canonical failure semantics and binds trajectories to packet IDs and causation chains; a trajectory proves execution history, never test passage, a distinction CRX enforces at the gate.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: the finally-persisted trajectory and typed-exit taxonomy are directly imitable; license must be verified before any code-level reuse.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: complete failure records are what make autonomous loops debuggable and their throughput claims auditable.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect src/minisweagent/agents/default.py for the finally-block trajectory save and the typed exit statuses; kill a run mid-iteration and confirm a trajectory file still exists with a typed abnormal exit.

LICENSE: AGPL-3.0 (LICENSE verified in repo; harvest as pattern, do not lift code into CRX)
PROBLEM: CI often tests a synthetic merge commit while the landing decision assumes the PR head was tested; and main-push CI often re-runs a full suite on a tree the merge queue already tested, wasting time or, worse, testing a different tree.
MECHANISM: scripts/ci/gate.py validates the complete CI plan before publishing the stable required check, using a per-event probe table: pull_request expects the changes probe, push expects already-tested, merge_group expects both. It is fail-closed: a probe that makes no decision raises ValueError; any job result mismatch raises. On success it writes tested-tree.txt containing the exact tree SHA that CI tested. scripts/ci/already-tested.sh implements the reuse probe: tree equality is the single safety property; a candidate prior run counts only if it recorded this exact tree. Missing/expired artifacts, old workflows, and API failures all fall back to full CI. A batched merge group combines trees no PR run ever had, so the comparison fails on its own and the full suite runs. ADR decisions/0050-a-merge-queue-tests-what-it-merges.md: the queue tests the merge tree and publishes the witness; main-push CI links the landed tree back to the queue run via the gh-readonly-queue/<base>/pr-<number>-<sha> branch and reruns only when it cannot prove landed tree equals tested tree. Caveat from the ADR: rulesets are external state and admin bypass exists, so the guarantee is disciplinary unless externally verified.
INVARIANT: Only complete CI may publish tested-tree evidence. Reuse requires exact tree equality with a recorded successful run; anything uncertain runs the full suite.
FAILURE_MODEL: Every uncertainty (missing artifact, expired run, API failure, old workflow) degrades to full CI, never to a skip. Probe indecision is a hard error, not a default-allow.
SECURITY_MODEL: The witness is published by the CI system itself after plan validation; consumers verify tree SHA equality rather than trusting labels or branch names.
SCALING_MODEL: The already-tested shortcut removes duplicate full-suite runs for up-to-date single-PR groups and for main pushes, cutting CI load without weakening the guarantee.
CRX_ANALOG: The merge gate publishes a tested-tree witness (tree SHA plus receipt refs) as a canonical event; post-merge verification compares the landed tree SHA to the witness and reruns checks only when equality cannot be proven.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX stores the witness as a canonical event with digest and causation to the gate run, making 'tested tree' a queryable fact rather than a CI artifact file.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the probe-table gate and tree-equality shortcut reimplement cleanly; AGPL means reimplement, never copy; the gh-readonly-queue branch naming is GitHub-specific and needs a CRX-native link.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: 'test what you land, and prove the landed tree is the tested tree' is the central correctness property of any merge factory.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect scripts/ci/gate.py PROBES table and the fail-closed ValueError paths; inspect scripts/ci/already-tested.sh for the tree-equality check and the full-CI fallback on missing artifacts; read the ADR for the merge_group tested-tree publication and main link-back.

PROBLEM: An agent's first solution attempt is often wrong or suboptimal; retry needs an independent judge with bounded cost, not infinite self-revision.
MECHANISM: sweagent/agent/reviewer.py: ReviewSubmission carries the trajectory, aggregate info, and model stats to an independent reviewer. The reviewer samples scores, rejects invalid or out-of-range scores, applies failure penalties, and can select the shortest solution among tied best scores (a simplicity bias). Retry loops are bounded by three independent budgets: attempt count, acceptance count, and cost.
INVARIANT: Review is performed by a separate reviewer invocation over the submission record, not by the author re-reading its own context. Score validation prevents a broken judge from approving everything.
FAILURE_MODEL: Invalid scores are rejected rather than averaged in. Budgets bound the loop; exhaustion is a terminal outcome with a record, not a hang.
SECURITY_MODEL: The reviewer consumes the trajectory artifact, not the author's live state; score ranges are validated before use.
SCALING_MODEL: Reviewer invocations are per-submission and parallelizable; cost budget caps spend per problem.
CRX_ANALOG: Reviewer as a separate WorkerRuntime role consuming patch artifact plus test receipts, emitting scored review with validated ranges; revision loops budgeted by attempts and cost with typed exhaustion.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX types reviewer scores into canonical review events and binds the simplicity-bias selection to an explicit, auditable rule rather than a reviewer-internal heuristic.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-medium: the separate-reviewer plus triple-budget pattern ports directly; CRX must type the review output as events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-high: independent review with bounded retry is the quality gate that keeps autonomous iteration from diverging or burning budget.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect sweagent/agent/reviewer.py for ReviewSubmission, score validation/rejection, failure penalties, shortest-among-ties selection, and the attempts/acceptance/cost retry bounds.

PROBLEM: A coder agent iterating against reviewer feedback can stall, repeating the same failed approach forever, or drown in unbounded round history.
MECHANISM: internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go: each revision round receives CoderInput with the round number, the prior round's diff, the verify check results, and the reviewer's issues; the reviewer returns a structured ReviewResult of ReviewIssues. Rounds are budgeted by MaxRounds. Stall detection fires on consecutive identical-fingerprint rounds, distinguishing 'the model needs another pass' from 'the coder cannot resolve what the reviewer is asking'. Escalation rounds surface the reviewer's outstanding issues as hard constraints that must each be addressed. Round history is compressed (CompressRounds) once it exceeds a threshold, keeping context bounded. Source: internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go, internal/orchestrator/history.go.
INVARIANT: Every revision round is grounded in the prior diff, the verify results, and the structured reviewer issues; no round proceeds on stale or missing feedback. History is bounded by compression, not by truncation.
FAILURE_MODEL: Stall is detected and escalated with hard constraints instead of looping forever. MaxRounds exhaustion is terminal with a full round record. Compression preserves issue counts and reviewer pushback as a brief, so escalation still sees what was rejected.
SECURITY_MODEL: Reviewer issues are structured data, not free-form prompt injection surface; escalation renders them as constraints, keeping the coder's instruction channel typed.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-task round loops are independent and parallelizable; history compression keeps token cost sublinear in round count.
CRX_ANALOG: WorkerRuntime reviewer role emits typed review issues as canonical events; the mutator's next attempt consumes the prior patch diff, test receipts, and open issues; stall detection and escalation are deterministic rules over event history.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX makes round fingerprints, stall detection, and escalation deterministic functions over canonical events, so any third party can replay why a loop stalled or escalated.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the round-input shape and stall/escalation logic port directly; CRX must define the fingerprint function and event schema.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: structured reviewer rounds with stall detection are the mechanism that makes agent iteration converge instead of spin.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect orchestrator.go for CoderInput (Issues, PrevDiff, PrevChecks), ReviewResult/ReviewIssue types, MaxRounds, stall-detection comments, and escalation-as-hard-constraints; inspect history.go CompressRounds for bounded history.

PROBLEM: Letting the same model both plan a change and apply it removes the checkpoint where intent can be inspected before mutation.
MECHANISM: aider/coders/architect_coder.py: the architect model proposes a plan; a separate editor coder/model performs the file mutation. Human confirmation is the default unless auto-accept is enabled. The editor receives clean message state and restricted configuration, so planning context does not leak into the mutation step.
INVARIANT: Planning and mutation are separate invocations with a confirmation checkpoint between them; the editor starts from clean state.
FAILURE_MODEL: A bad plan is caught at the confirmation checkpoint before any file is touched. Editor misbehavior is bounded by its restricted configuration.
SECURITY_MODEL: The editor's restricted configuration and clean state limit what a compromised or confused planner can cause it to do; human confirmation is the default-deny.
SCALING_MODEL: Two model calls per change instead of one; the editor call is narrow and cheaper than the planning call.
CRX_ANALOG: Narrow authority separation as a general pattern: distinct roles for proposing, mutating, and reviewing, each with least-privilege context. Useful where a confirmation checkpoint must exist between intent and mutation.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: This is planner/editor separation, NOT reviewer/author separation; do not mislabel it as independent review. In CRX it informs role least-privilege design, not the review gate.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: it is a design pattern for role separation, not a component to port.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: a cheap, proven way to insert an inspectable checkpoint between intent and mutation; prevents an entire class of 'the model did what it planned without anyone seeing the plan' failures.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect aider/coders/architect_coder.py for the architect-plan then editor-mutate flow, the default human confirmation, and the editor's clean message state and restricted configuration.

PROBLEM: Merging a PR whose approvals, checks, or head are stale or incomplete silently lands unreviewed or untested code.
MECHANISM: lib/worker/batcher.ex, patch_preflight/3, requires all of: no CI-skip marker, no blocking labels, no configured status in error, no configured status still running, every required status present, review threshold satisfied, no changes-requested review, CODEOWNERS approvals where enabled, and approval tied to the current commit where up_to_date_approvals is enabled. Any unmet condition blocks the patch from entering the batch; the gate is evaluated at batch assembly time, not at approval time.
INVARIANT: Approval is only meaningful when bound to the exact commit being merged; required checks must be present and green at gate time, not merely at some earlier time.
FAILURE_MODEL: Each unmet condition is a distinct block reason; the patch waits or is rejected, never merged hopefully. Stale approvals (commit moved) fail the up-to-date check.
SECURITY_MODEL: CI-skip markers and blocking labels are deny signals the gate honors; CODEOWNERS enforcement is configurably mandatory.
SCALING_MODEL: Preflight is per-patch at batch assembly; cheap checks gate entry to the expensive batch CI run.
CRX_ANALOG: Merge gate preflight as a checklist evaluated at candidate-tree assembly: approvals bound to exact tree SHA, required receipts present and green, no deny markers, scope-conflict check; every unmet condition a typed block event.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX replaces GitHub-specific signals (labels, statuses, CODEOWNERS) with canonical equivalents: approval events referencing tree SHAs, test receipt events, deny-marker events, scope ownership records.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the checklist logic ports directly; CRX must define its canonical approval and receipt event schemas.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: the preflight checklist is the highest-leverage defect filter in the lane; most bad landings are stale or incomplete gates, not bad code.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect lib/worker/batcher.ex patch_preflight/3 for each required condition and the up_to_date_approvals commit binding; attempt to batch a patch whose head moved after approval and confirm it is blocked.

PROBLEM: Green checks on individual PR heads do not prove the merged result works; integration failures hide in the combination.
MECHANISM: start_waiting_batch builds a staging tree by merging the batch's patches onto the current target branch head, then CI statuses attach to that synthesized batch commit, not to the individual PR heads. complete_batch/3 pushes the exact tested batch commit to the target ref only after the status summary is :ok. The invariant, stated as the core of the design: author PR checks are insufficient; build and test the exact integration tree against current trunk, then land that exact SHA.
INVARIANT: What is tested (the synthesized batch commit on current trunk) is bit-for-bit what lands. No re-merge, no re-cherry-pick between test and land.
FAILURE_MODEL: Batch CI failure blocks the whole batch; the divider then bisects to isolate the failing patch rather than discarding all successful work (see BORS-FAILURE-BISECTION).
SECURITY_MODEL: The staging commit is synthesized by the gate service, not by patch authors; authors cannot substitute a different tree between test and land.
SCALING_MODEL: Batching amortizes one CI run over many patches; bisection cost is logarithmic in batch size on failure.
CRX_ANALOG: The CRX merge gate synthesizes the candidate integration tree on the current base, runs required checks against that exact tree, publishes a tested-tree witness, and CAS-lands that exact SHA.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX adds the tested-tree witness as a canonical event so post-merge verification can prove landed-equals-tested without re-running CI.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the synthesize-test-land-exact-SHA pipeline is the core of the CRX merge gate; the divider/bisector ports as the batch-failure recovery.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Very high: this single invariant eliminates the largest class of integration escapes in any merge factory.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect batcher.ex for the staging-commit synthesis and status attachment to the batch commit; inspect complete_batch/3 for the push-only-on-:ok and exact-SHA landing; confirm no re-merge occurs between test and push.

PROBLEM: A task branch approved and verified against an old base may be semantically different after rebasing onto a moved integration branch; mechanical rebase success does not imply the change is still correct or still approved.
MECHANISM: MergeRequest carries ReReview and ReVerify hooks. After the rebase path: SyncWorktree moves the still-alive task worktree to the rebased tip (so gates run against the right tree AND the project's installed dependencies, which only exist there); the queue diffs the rebased tree against staging and, if the normalized diff differs from the approved diff, calls ReReview(newDiff), which must return approved=true or the merge blocks with CodeRebaseReviewRejected; then ReVerify() runs the project's verify checks against the rebased state ('a rebase can succeed mechanically while still breaking tests'), blocking with CodeRebaseVerifyFailed on failure. Only then does the CAS advance staging. Source: internal/orchestrator/mergeq.go, MergeRequest struct and process().
INVARIANT: A stale-base rebase re-earns both approval (if the diff changed) and verification (always) before landing. Review binds to diff content, not to branch identity.
FAILURE_MODEL: Re-review rejection and re-verify failure are typed blocks; the staging ref is untouched and the queue restores its checkout. The task worktree stays alive through the hooks via the Cleanup callback, which runs exactly once after the ack.
SECURITY_MODEL: Hooks run against the rebased tree in the task's own worktree with its real dependencies; the queue's detached checkout cannot pass dependency-needing checks, which is why SyncWorktree exists.
SCALING_MODEL: Re-review/re-verify run serially per queued merge; they only trigger on the rebase path, so the common fast path stays cheap.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX merge gate: on stale base, rebase the patch, re-run the reviewer over the new diff when it changed, re-run required test receipts on the rebased tree, then CAS-land; each step a canonical event.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX types ReReview/ReVerify as separate canonical events with their own receipts, so the re-earned approval is auditable independently of the original review.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the hook sequence ports directly; CRX must wire ReVerify into its test-receipt machinery and ReReview into its reviewer role.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: closes the 'rebased but never re-checked' hole that defeats every other gate in the lane.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect mergeq.go for the normalize-diff comparison gating ReReview, the ReVerify call after rebase, SyncWorktree ordering, and the typed block codes; rebase a task onto a conflicting-but-auto-resolvable base change and confirm re-review triggers when the diff changes.

PROBLEM: The target branch moves between batch test and batch land; the push fails non-fast-forward. The content passed tests, so discarding or bisecting the batch would waste verified work.
MECHANISM: On non-fast-forward push failure, the batch is cloned/requeued against the new base without bisecting, because the content passed but the base changed: stale base is not bad content. Unknown push failures do not retry indefinitely; push retries use bounded exponential backoff.
INVARIANT: A non-FF landing failure is classified as stale base (retryable by requeue), never as content failure. Bounded retries; unknown failures escalate, not loop.
FAILURE_MODEL: Non-FF: requeue against new base, no bisect. Unknown push failure: bounded exponential backoff, then typed failure. The batch's tested content is preserved, not discarded.
SECURITY_MODEL: Requeue rebuilds the batch against the new base through the normal gate path; no shortcut around preflight.
SCALING_MODEL: Requeue cost is one more batch cycle; bisection is skipped, saving logarithmic work that would have been wasted on good content.
CRX_ANALOG: Non-fast-forward at land time is a typed retryable stale-base state: rebase the tested content onto the new base, re-verify, re-land; never bisect good content for a moved base.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX emits the non-FF outcome as a canonical event with the expected-vs-actual ref SHAs, making stale-base retries auditable and distinguishable from content failures.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: the classification (non-FF = stale base, not bad content) and bounded-retry discipline port directly.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-high: prevents the factory from destroying verified work on every trunk movement; essential for high-trunk-velocity operation.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect batcher.ex push-failure handling for the non-FF requeue path and the absence of bisection on that path; inspect the bounded exponential backoff on push retries.

PROBLEM: A batch of many patches fails its integration CI; discarding the whole batch wastes all the good patches' verified work and re-serializes everything.
MECHANISM: lib/worker/batcher/divider.ex: failed batches are split/bisected to isolate the failing patch(es) rather than discarding all successful work. Cancellation preserves and retries uncanceled patches, so an aborted batch does not lose its good members.
INVARIANT: Batch failure isolates blame to the failing subset; verified-good patches are never punished for a neighbor's failure.
FAILURE_MODEL: Bisection is logarithmic in batch size; each sub-batch re-runs the gate path. Uncanceled patches survive cancellation and are retried, not dropped.
SECURITY_MODEL: Bisection reuses the same preflight and test-exact-tree path; no weakened checks on sub-batches.
SCALING_MODEL: Failure cost scales logarithmically, not linearly, with batch size; the common all-green path pays no bisection cost.
CRX_ANALOG: Integration batch failure triggers a bisect over the batch's patches, each sub-batch re-entering the merge gate; good patches land, bad patches get typed failure events with their receipts attached.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX records each bisection step as canonical events, so the blame assignment is replayable and the good patches' landing is causally linked to the original batch.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the divider logic ports directly; CRX must integrate it with its event-sourced queue so sub-batches are traceable.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-high: at batch scale, bisection is what keeps one bad patch from halting the entire factory.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect lib/worker/batcher/divider.ex for the split logic; fail one patch in a multi-patch batch and confirm the good patches land while only the failing patch is isolated.

PROBLEM: After the merge queue lands a tree, main-push CI must establish that the landed tree is exactly the tree the queue tested, without blindly re-running everything or blindly trusting.
MECHANISM: scripts/ci/already-tested.sh on the push event (main): the queue tested this tree under a gh-readonly-queue/<base>/pr-<number>-<sha> branch moments ago, so that queue run is the proof; a PR merged outside the queue still reaches its own pull_request run as before. Main reruns full CI only when it cannot prove the landed tree equals the tested tree. scripts/ci/gate.py enforces that only complete CI may publish the tested-tree evidence consumed by this link-back.
INVARIANT: Post-merge confidence rests on proven tree equality with a recorded successful run, not on branch names, labels, or recency. Unprovable equality runs the full suite.
FAILURE_MODEL: Any gap in the proof chain (no queue run, mismatched tree, expired artifact) degrades to full CI on main, never to assumed-green.
SECURITY_MODEL: The link-back resolves through the queue's own branch namespace and recorded tree SHAs; out-of-queue merges fall back to their own PR runs, so bypassing the queue cannot inherit its proof.
SCALING_MODEL: The common case (queue-landed, tree provably equal) skips duplicate full CI on main, removing the merge queue's main-branch CI tax.
CRX_ANALOG: Post-merge verification compares the landed tree SHA to the gate's tested-tree witness event; on equality, record verified-landed; on mismatch or missing witness, run the full check suite and raise a typed incident.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX makes the link-back a canonical event comparison (landed SHA vs witness SHA) rather than a CI script querying the hosting API, and adds runtime probes as separate receipt-producing steps on top.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: the tree-equality link-back reimplements cleanly; AGPL means reimplement, never copy; the gh-readonly-queue naming is GitHub-specific.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-high: proves the factory's central promise after every landing, and removes duplicate main-branch CI when the proof holds.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Inspect scripts/ci/already-tested.sh push-event branch for the queue-run lookup and tree-equality requirement; land a tree the queue never tested and confirm main runs full CI instead of skipping.
